inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: During the investigation, it was found that the caregiver did not use good judgment when she approached the caregiver and raised her voice in front of the children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: Clorox wipes was observed on the diapering table. This was corrected when the caregiver removed the wipes out of the reach of the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: An old couch/chair was observed torn and poses a safety risk to the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Planned Activities Designed to Meet Individual Needs: One classroom did not have enough activities for the children to play with. The caregiver had provided activities without allowing the children to choose
occurrences.violation_type_title: Planned Activities Designed to Meet Individual Needs (26 TAC §746.2201)

occurrences.finding: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean: Several caulking spots were seen throughout one of the classrooms, in another room, the door was observed and needs to be wiped down.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Floors, ceilings and Walls in Good Repair and Clean (26 TAC §746.3407(9))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check determination - If ineligible then you must immediately remove subject from operation and confirm to CBCU receipt of notice letter: the operation was not following the conditions of the background when an individual without a background was allowed inside the operation while having access to the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check determination - If ineligible then you must immediately remove subject from operation and confirm to CBCU receipt of notice letter (26 TAC §745.635(2))

occurrences.finding: Report Unsafe Facility Occurrence: During an investigation inspection, it was found, the operation did not report to childcare regulations an occurrence that rendered the facility unsafe.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Unsafe Facility Occurrence (26 TAC §746.305(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: The operation has been educated on background check guidelines and how to determine if and when a person is eligible to be present at the operation. With this knowledge, staff did not use good judgment when they knowingly allowed and facilitated the presence of a person with ineligible conditions to be present at the operation while children were in care.   The operation would not report this interaction to childcare regulations.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check determination - If ineligible then you must immediately remove subject from operation and confirm to CBCU receipt of notice letter: The operation did not follow the conditions of the background unit by allowing a person deemed ineligible to be present and inside the operation during operating hours and while children were in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check determination - If ineligible then you must immediately remove subject from operation and confirm to CBCU receipt of notice letter (26 TAC §745.635(2))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: A caregiver was observed pulling a small child up by the arm and sitting the child down aggressively on the bottom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: AP Cribs - Only Snug Fitting Sheet and Crib Mattress Cover Allowed if Infant Younger than 12 Months of Age: A child was observed in a crib with a boppie pad and a crib mobile. This was corrected when the caregiver removed the items from the crib.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Cribs - Only Snug Fitting Sheet and Crib Mattress Cover Allowed if Infant Younger than 12 Months of Age (26 TAC §746.2415(b))

occurrences.finding: Determining Child/Caregiver Ratios - Basis: A caregiver was observed with 9 children, bringing the group out of ratio by 5. This was corrected when the second caregiver returned to the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Determining Child/Caregiver Ratios - Basis (26 TAC §746.1507(1))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area - Space to Walk Between Cribs, Cots or Mats: In three of the classrooms, the nap mats were observed to not have enough space to walk between. The children were observed touching each cot or blanket of another child.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area - Space to Walk Between Cribs, Cots or Mats (26 TAC §746.2403(5))

occurrences.finding: Requirements for Feeding Infants - No Walking or Sleeping with Bottle or Cup: A child was observed to have a bottle in the crib while asleep. The bottle was removed from the crib.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - No Walking or Sleeping with Bottle or Cup (26 TAC §746.2419(7))

occurrences.finding: Covering Infant's Head or Crib: Children must never allowed to sleep with a blanket or other coverings over their heads.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Covering Infant's Head or Crib (26 TAC §746.2429)

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A child was left on the playground unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation did not report to regulations a situation that placed a child a risk while in care within the time allowed in the standards.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: A child in care was involved in an at-risk situation and the parent was not notified.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Parent right to enter and examine operation without advance notice: Parents were observed not being able to enter the rear of the building where children are being provided care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parent right to enter and examine operation without advance notice (26 TAC §746.521(1))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired: A wall outlet was observed to be broken and accessible to children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance Procedures for Active Play - Hazards Removed or Repaired (26 TAC §746.4751(c))

occurrences.finding: Garbage Inaccessible to Children; Maintained in Sanitary Manner: A trash can without a lid was observed in the classroom where children were being provided care. This was corrected when the trash can was emptied and removed from the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Garbage Inaccessible to Children; Maintained in Sanitary Manner (26 TAC §746.3407(8))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Two caregivers were observed laying down near children during nap time. The caregivers were covered with blankets and had placed a small covering over the lamp used for lighting.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records: 3 new staff did not have signed notarized affidavits or the required pre-application affidavits.   4 of the 5 personnel files did not have enough annual training hours to evaluate,   Staff records did not have completed preservice training that was documented.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records (26 TAC §746.801(3))

occurrences.finding: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes: The operation had not practiced fire drills during  the month of September.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Fire Drill Monthly - Exit in 3 Minutes (26 TAC §746.5205(1))

occurrences.finding: AP Background ck determination - If provisionally eligible w/conditions or eligible w/conditions you must restrict duties per conditions/restrictions: The operation was found to have violated conditions that CBCU placed on a person?s presence at the operation when the person was found to be the only caregiver in a classroom with children in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background ck determination - If provisionally eligible w/conditions or eligible w/conditions you must restrict duties per conditions/restrictions (26 TAC §745.635(3))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: The grass had not been cut. This was corrected during the inspection when the lawn man cut the grass. Broken outdoor toys were observed and corrected when removed from the playground. A broken urinal was observed, and a repair order was made. Lysol wipes was observed on a diaper station. There were no children in the room, and the wipes were removed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Electronic or Battery-Operated Carbon Monoxide Detector-Document Test Date, Battery Installation Date, and Staff Name Testing and Installation: The carbon monoxide detector test had not been conducted or documented. This was corrected during the inspection, when the detector was tested and documented.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic or Battery-Operated Carbon Monoxide Detector-Document Test Date, Battery Installation Date, and Staff Name Testing and Installation (26 TAC §746.5537(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: Four concrete liners were observed overlapping the play area and in the use zones.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Snug Fitting Sheets: Cribs were observed with sheets that did not fit snugly on the mattress.     This was corrected during the inspection, when tight fitting sheet were placed on the mattresses.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Snug Fitting Sheets (26 TAC §746.2409(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment: During the inspection, children were observed sleeping on the floor with no cot or mat. Children were observed sleeping on torn mats.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maintenance of Building, Grounds and Equipment (26 TAC §746.3407)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: This standard has been reviewed and found to be deficient. the caregiver without malice or anger, did not use good judgement when picking a child in care up by the arm causing injury.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Snug Fitting Sheets: During the inspection, 2 children were observed asleep in cribs with loose fitted sheets.  7 cribs in total were observed with sheets that were not tight fitting.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Cribs - Snug Fitting Sheets (26 TAC §746.2409(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Adequate Lighting During Naptime: During nap time a room with 2-3 year olds was too dark to see the children napping, therefore supervision could not be maintained.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Adequate Lighting During Naptime (26 TAC §746.2911)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers- Supervision of Children: A caregiver in a room with 23 month olds - 3 year olds did nont know the ages of the children care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: In a room with children ages 3-5 years it was found there was a bottle of bleach water stored in reach of children.    In the school age room there was trash accessible to children.    In a room with children ages 23 months - 3 years there was a caregivers purse stored on a couch that was accessible to children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: 5 children's files were reviewed, 1 was found to have no shot records, and one was found to be missing an MMR and a varicella vaccine.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Arrangement of Napping Equipment -All Children Supervised: in a room with 14 month old children it was found that 3 children were napping with their heads covered by their blankets.    In another room with children ages 23 months - 3 years 2 children were sleeping with their heads covered by their heads.    This was corrected at time of inspection when the caregiver took the blankets off each of their heads.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Arrangement of Napping Equipment -All Children Supervised (26 TAC §746.2909(5))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: An employee was present at the operation prior to  receiving an eligibility notification.    The employee did leave the operation while the inspection was being conducted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: All 7 employee files reviewed did not have training on the following topics:   Administering medication, if applicable  Preventing and responding to emergencies due to food or an allergic reaction   Understanding building and physical premises safety, including identification and protection from hazards that can cause bodily injury such as electrical hazards, bodies of water, and vehicular traffic  and Handling, storing, and disposing of hazardous materials
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Reduction of child/caregiver naptime ratio by 50% allowed, If 13 or more children in care, children are 18 mo. or older and other standards met: There were 10 children 13 months - 20 months with a specified age group of 14 month and 1 caregiver in one room. 8 of the children were sleeping and 2 of the children were awake.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Reduction of child/caregiver naptime ratio by 50% allowed, If 13 or more children in care, children are 18 mo. or older and other standards met (26 TAC §746.1613(a))

occurrences.finding: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - is equipped in each vehicle: Both Vans used to transport children do not have child safety alarms.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Electronic Child Safety Alarm - is equipped in each vehicle (26 TAC §746.5625(a))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent: From interviews and the investigation it was found that the operation did not provide the incident report with in the required time frame.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)
